claim: For connected finite simple undirected graphs, compare two nontrivial bipartitions of the same graph, requiring each side of each bipartition to contain at least two vertices and each bipartition to have positive Newman–Girvan modularity \(Q\). Let \(\operatorname{Ncut}(A,B)=c/\operatorname{vol}(A)+c/\operatorname{vol}(B)\), where \(c\) is the number of cut edges. For every graph on at most \(5\) vertices, larger modularity never ranks one admissible bipartition above another while normalized cut, which is minimized, ranks it below. Six vertices are sharp. Among all connected labeled graphs on \(6\) vertices there are \(420\) strict reversing partition pairs, collapsing to exactly two isomorphism classes of graph together with an unordered pair of bipartitions. One class is \(K_4\) minus an edge with a pendant path of length \(2\) attached to one endpoint of the missing edge; its reversing splits have \((Q,\operatorname{Ncut})=(19/98,14/33)\) and \((10/49,7/12)\). The other class is \(K_4\) and \(K_3\) sharing exactly one vertex; its reversing splits have \((Q,\operatorname{Ncut})=(10/81,9/14)\) and \((1/6,2/3)\). In both classes modularity prefers the second split while normalized cut prefers the first. For any bipartition with side volumes \(a,b\) in a graph with \(m\) edges, the exact identity \(Q=ab(1-\operatorname{Ncut})/(2m^2)\) explains the mechanism: the objectives agree at fixed volume balance but can reverse when the balance factor \(ab\) changes.
integrity: The proof derives an exact algebraic identity between bipartition modularity, normalized cut, and the side-volume product, then exhaustively enumerates every connected labeled graph through six vertices and all admissible bipartitions using exact rational arithmetic. The 420 labeled six-vertex reversal pairs are canonically quotiented under all vertex relabelings and partition symmetries to two classes.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns connected simple undirected graphs, two-way partitions with at least two vertices per side, and positive Newman–Girvan modularity. It compares the exact discrete objectives, not spectral relaxations, multiway partitions, or all larger graphs.
title: Six vertices are the sharp positive-modularity reversal boundary for modularity and normalized cut
